about: A mark-for-op set (mark untagged instances, stop what is marked after 3 days, unmark what gets tagged in time): different filters, one constraint, so one bullet.

source.name: ec2-owner-stop
source.description: Stop instances marked for having no owner.

source.name: ec2-owner-unmark
source.description: Unmark instances that now have an owner.

controls.output: - EC2 instances without an `Owner` tag are flagged and marked to be stopped in 3 days; tagging one in time removes the mark. Instances with `Owner` pass. MEDIUM, ORG; marks, then stops what is still marked. acme:ec2-owner-mark@1 acme:ec2-owner-stop@1 acme:ec2-owner-unmark@1

- EC2 instances with neither an `Owner` tag nor a `c7n_status` tag are flagged. Instances with either tag pass. Medium, ORG: flagged instances are marked for stop with 3 days' notice, and instances still marked are stopped. Low, ORG: instances that have both `Owner` and `c7n_status` have `c7n_status` removed. acme:ec2-owner-mark@1, acme:ec2-owner-stop@1, acme:ec2-owner-unmark@1

- EC2 instances without an `Owner` tag are marked to be stopped in 3 days. Tagged ones pass. MEDIUM, ORG. acme:ec2-owner-mark@1
- EC2 instances marked for stopping are stopped. Others pass. MEDIUM, ORG; stops them. acme:ec2-owner-stop@1
- EC2 instances tagged `Owner` after marking are unmarked. LOW, ORG. acme:ec2-owner-unmark@1
- EC2 instances without an `Owner` tag are flagged and stopped (three policies). Tagged instances pass. MEDIUM, ORG; stops them. acme:ec2-owner-mark@1 acme:ec2-owner-stop@1 acme:ec2-owner-unmark@1
